narrative:
The model estimates a 73% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the organization has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned about investing in someone likely to depart soon.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor. With 6-10 years of overall experience, you fall into a group that the model associates with higher turnover risk compared to the majority of employees predicted to stay, who more often have only 1-5 years of total experience. This pushes the prediction noticeably toward leaving.

Second, the fact that you have received other job opportunities while working here is the next most influential element. Having external offers signals to the model a realistic path to departure, strongly increasing the likelihood of leaving.

Third, your relatively short tenure in your current role (1-5 years) also contributes to the prediction of leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have built longer histories at their organizations.

Taken together, these factors outweigh many positive signals in your profile, such as high job support, recognition, emotional commitment, and satisfaction with your environment. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, while you may want to reflect on whether your external opportunities better align with your long-term goals.
